newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures were both expected to open steady to 0.200 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover selling in live cattle was expected to stem from the weak undertone to fed cattle markets and mixed boxed beef markets. Packers continued to lower their bids for fed cattle and some cattle may have traded at $66 per cwt late Tuesday, another $1 lower, analysts said.
However, the USDA Cold Storage report Tuesday showed a decline in beef stocks despite increased cow slaughter and this was viewed as mildly bullish to futures, they said.

Feeder cattle futures may continue under pressure following the weakness in fed cattle markets. Although corn futures broke late Tuesday after feeder cattle had closed, a higher call for corn futures Wednesday morning will likely weigh on feeders, they said
The CME feeder cattle index showed a small rise and will likely have little effect on the market, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.04 to $76.37 per cwt.
